notes:
Need to search first.I couldn't write these notes. None of my attempts to reach the source sites worked, so I have no material from any of the approved pages.

**What happened:**
- I tried to open the Psalm 91 pages directly on enduringword.com, biblehub.com (Ellicott, Gill, Pulpit Commentary), preceptaustin.org and netbible.org. The tool refused every one because it only opens addresses that have first turned up in a search result.
- I then tried to run the searches, but the first batch (16 at once) hit the search limit. The smaller retry was blocked because I had used up all my tool calls for this turn.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never to fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written any verse notes, URLs or tradition comparisons, because none of it would have come from a page I read.

**What I'd do next time (send the request again, or just say "try again"):**
1. Search first, a few searches at a time, so the pages can then be opened. I'd start with:
   - Enduring Word on Psalm 91
   - Ellicott, Gill and Pulpit Commentary on BibleHub/StudyLight
   - Precept Austin
   - Spurgeon's *Treasury of David*
2. Then search for the topics most likely to show real differences of view:
   - Satan quoting vv. 11–12 when he tempts Jesus (Matthew 4 / Luke 4).
   - Whether vv. 3–10 promise physical safety from plague. Pages written during COVID on gotquestions.org, desiringgod.org, thegospelcoalition.org and ligonier.org should be useful here.
   - "Word of faith" teaching on claiming the psalm's protection.
   - Catholic and Orthodox use of the psalm in evening prayer (newadvent.org, catholic.com, oca.org).
   - The NET Bible notes on the Hebrew words for "terror," "pestilence" and the animals in v. 13.
3. Write the verse-by-verse notes using only what those pages say, with a URL after every point.
